chunks: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Inform me of the most excellent of the timings for the Fajr salat. So he said: At the emergence of dawn.
Indeed, God, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'and the morning recitation; surely the recitation at dawn was always witnessed'

— meaning the Fajr salat. The angels of the night witness it and the angels of the day. So when the servant prays the morning prayer at the emergence of dawn, it is affirmed for him twice — recorded by the angels of the night and the angels of the day.

key_terms.المواقيت: The prescribed times (mawaqit) — the appointed time-windows within which each prayer is valid
key_terms.طلوع الفجر: The emergence/rising of dawn — the specific moment when the first light of day appears on the horizon
key_terms.مرتين: Twice — the doubled recording of merit when the prayer is performed precisely at dawn's emergence
key_terms.مشهوداً: 'Witnessed' — the Quranic adjective that the Imam interprets as referring to the presence of two groups of angels

ai.seo_question: What is the best time to pray Fajr salat according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Ishaq ibn Ammar asked Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about the optimal time for Fajr prayer and received the answer: at the moment of dawn's emergence. The Imam supported this ruling by citing Quran 17:78, which describes the dawn recitation (i.e., Fajr prayer) as 'witnessed' by both the angels of the night and the angels of the day. By praying at this exact transitional moment, a worshipper's prayer is recorded by two groups of angels simultaneously, thus earning double merit. This hadith grounds a jurisprudential ruling in Quranic exegesis, reflecting a key feature of Shia fiqh methodology.
